messages:
maria: Heads up — Support just escalated: Customer org 'acme-corp' saw quota graphs showing another org's usage (org id 7421) in the Insights dashboard at ~10:03am PT.
aj: whoa. any reproducible steps?
maria: Support said: login -> Insights -> time range 7d -> quota panel shows spikes that don't match their billing. They took a screenshot.
kevin: linking the screenshot in case helpful: https://redwood.slack/img/priv/anon-screenshot.png
chris: first guess: routing/header affinity got weird during today's rollout of route-mux v2? we had a header normalization change pushed in canary.
amj: @aj (typo) — I think you mean @aj.
aj: lol yes. I pushed the header normalizer patch to the router canary at 09:50. It strips duplicate headers and canonicalizes casing. Could that drop `x-redwood-org` in some edge path?
kevin: Support log shows proxy forwarded: x-redwood-org: 8319 for most calls, but the dashboard queries show org 7421.
maria: ops timeline: canary to 10% at 09:50, 50% at 10:10 per deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: deploy v2-route-mux started at 09:49:58; canary 10% at 09:50:12; rollout paused 50% at 10:10:03 due to errors (automated).
chris: hm if the router canonicalizes headers, our prefetch/cache key uses both `x-redwood-org` and `x-rw-affinity`. If one of them is missing or renamed, we can hit the wrong cache shard. That would return stale panel data for the wrong org.
aj: checking the router commit — the PR changed header merging to `map[string]lowercase(key)] = lastValue` which could drop header case variations but shouldn't drop the header entirely. But there's a separate path for internal-adapters where we copied headers into metadata and used `x-rw-affinity` as the source-of-truth. I see a bug: when `x-redwood-org` was present and `x-rw-affinity` was not, the metadata merge set org to empty if the header list was empty for that adapter.
kevin: pulling traces for requests around 10:02 for acme-corp.
kevin: trace: GET /api/insights/panels/quota -> routed to backend instance b-13 -> cache-key: panel:v1|org:7421|panel:quota|range:7d -> cache hit -> served 200.
maria: so a request from acme (8319) somehow produced cache key with 7421.
chris: possible race where adapter A stripped header, adapter B set affinity from a previous request on the same connection. connection-level metadata leak?
aj: we recently switched to keepalive pooling for internal gRPC connections to improve latency — connection reuse might mean metadata sticky state if we accidentally used mutable per-connection state for last-seen-org.
kevin: searching code: `connection.state.lastOrg = orgHeader` in router/proxy/conn_state.go — that's mutable and not cleared on request start in the version deployed in canary. Oops.
amaria: That matches the symptom: reuse + mutable per-connection state + header normalization change -> some requests end up with the previous request's lastOrg.
chris: if that's true, quota graphs could show other orgs when a cache entry for org B exists on that connection.
aj: mitigation: roll back the canary to remove the header normalization + keepalive change. Also add a quick patch to clear `connection.state.lastOrg` at request start.
kevin: I can revert the canary via the rollout console. Who wants to own the patch?
achris: I can open a small PR to clear lastOrg and add a unit test for connection reuse.
maria: priority = P0 for customer impact (duplicate org data visible). Support is preparing comms.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2028 - console quota panel cross-org exposure. Severity: medium. creators: maria.
aj: rolling back canary now.
deploy-bot: rollback v2-route-mux to v1 at 10:12:18; canary 10% reverted.
kevin: after rollback, I still see some traces (10:05--10:11 window) with bad cache-key. But new requests after 10:13 look clean.
maria: Support confirmed acme-corp saw cleanup after 10:15. They're waiting for root cause explanation.
chris: next steps: (1) revert keepalive pooling change or make connection state immutable per-request (PR #3871) — chris owns. (2) add request-start clearing of per-connection mutable metadata — chris/aj pair. (3) add guard in cache-key generator to assert orgID != empty and fallback to auth token parsing to avoid cross-org cache hits — aj owns. (4) add telemetry: tag every cache hit with origin-org and resolved-org to detect future divergence — kevin owns.
aj: I'll submit the cache-key assert and telemetry patch today.
kevin: I'll add an opt-in alert on telemetry divergence (resolved_org != origin_org) with 1m/5m windows.
maria: also add a rollout playbook entry: when changing header handling or connection reuse, run targeted load tests simulating rapid org switches and multi-tenant cache keys.
achris: opened PR 3871 with clearing and tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/3871
aj: opened PR 3872 for cache-key guard + telemetry tags.
kevin: alert rule draft: name: cache-org-divergence; query: sum(rate(cache_hits{origin_org!="" AND resolved_org!=""} >/m)) by (project) > 0.1 -> paging. will refine.
maria: thanks team. Can we have a postmortem doc by EOD tomorrow with timeline, root cause, and customer comm text?
chris: yes. I'll ping when PR merged.
kevin: FYI, I'll rotate the cache shard keys for the affected time window to reduce chance of stale wrong-org data lingering in edge caches (cache purge job queued).
amaria: support will follow up with acme-corp and include cleanup ETA. :thumbsup:
aj: tl;dr: keepalive + mutable per-connection lastOrg + header normalization change in canary -> some requests inherited a previous request's org, generating wrong cache keys -> cross-org quota panels. Rollback done, patches in flight.
chris: any other suspects (telemetry sampling, metrics pipeline)?
kevin: telemetry showed the divergence spike matching canary timeline only. sampling is fine. pipeline didn't alter org ids.
maria: OK closing thread here. Please paste postmortem link when ready.
